MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING

This Memorandum of Understanding (this “MOU”) is entered into as of this 10th day of

October, 2025 (the “Effective Date”), by and between:

WESTERN POCAHONTAS PROPERTIES LIMITED PARTNERSHIP (“WPPLP”), a Delaware

limited partnership; and

FUNDAMENTAL DATA LLC (“Fundamental”), a Delaware limited liability company.

(Each a “Party” and collectively, the “Parties”).

RECITALS

A. The Parties are party to that certain Development Agreement dated July 19, 2024 (the

“DA’).

B. The Parties have entered into the First Amendment to the DA, dated October 1, 2025 (the

“First Amendment”), which extended the Feasibility Period and amended the Distribution

Payments provisions.

C. The Parties have negotiated and agreed upon certain additional commercial terms not

covered by the First Amendment that are intended to be incorporated into the DA and the

related Site Control Agreements (as defined in the DA) through future definitive agreements.

D. The Parties now desire to enter into this MOU to formally record their mutual intent to

negotiate and ‘agree upon definitive amendments to the DA and Site Control Agreements

related to these remaining terms.

AGREEMENT OF INTENT TO NEGOTIATE

1. Purpose. The Parties hereby confirm their mutual and non-binding intent to

negotiate, draft, and execute a Second Amendment to the DA, or other appropriate

definitive agreements, that will formalize the key outstanding commercial terms

identified herein.

2. Topics for Future Amendment. The Parties agree to negotiate in good faith the

following principal commercial terms for inclusion in future definitive agreements:

(a) Permits Upon Expiration of the Development Agreement. In the event that

Fundamental does not (i) provide notice of its intent to close under any Site

Control Agreement and post the deposit pursuant to the new Section 10 of the

DA by September 30, 2026, and (ii) close under a Site Control Agreement by

December 31, 2026, then Fundamental shall assign, transfer, or otherwise

grant the rights to any permits obtained for the Project to WPPLP. This

provision shall be documented through an assignment, limited power of

attorney, or other documents to be negotiated by the parties and acceptable

to counsel.

(b) Communications. Fundamental will allow WPPLP non-exclusive right to

access any internet point of presence (“POP”) established at the Project and

under the control of Fundamental. WPPLP shall comply with any

interconnection standards applicable to the POP, including rules established

to maintain system security.

Natural Gas. Subject to compliance with West Virginia law and, if applicable,

the rules of any administrative agency of the state, including the Public Service

Commission, Fundamental shall agree to allow WPPLP to connect to any

private gas system constructed by or for Fundamental and purchase “excess”

natural gas from Fundamental or its suppliers. Inno event, shall Fundamental

be required to sell gas to WPPLP if such sale would cause Fundamental to

become a “public utility” under WV law.

(d) Power. Subject to compliance with West Virginia law and, if applicable, the

rules of any administrative agency of the state including the West Virignia

Pubtic Service Commission, Fundamental shall agree to allow WPPLP to

connect to our internal power system at its applicable voltage (currently

planned to be 138 kV) and purchase power under terms no less favorable than

those provided to data centers operating within the Project. Inno event, shall

Fundamental be required to sell power to WPPLP if such sale would (1) violate

the provisions of the Power Generation and Consumption Act of 2025, or (2)

cause Fundamental to become a “public utility” under WV law.

(e) Water. Subject to compliance with West Virginia law and, if applicable, the

rules of any administrative agency of the state including the West Virignia

Public Service Commission, Fundamental shall agree to allow WPPLP to

connect to our internal water system and purchase water under terms no less

favorable than those provided to data centers operating within the Project. In

no event, shall Fundamental be required to sell water to WPPLP if such sale

would cause Fundamental to become a “public utility” under WV law.

Fundamental will make no representations regarding water quality or warranty

with respect to fitness for any purpose, including agriculture or human

consumption.

Fundamental’s obligations under this Section 2 shall be performed at no cost to

Fundamental and any expenses incurred by Fundamental in connection with these

obligations shall be for the account of WPPLP.

3. Project Status Updates. Fundamental will provide WPPLP monthly updates

regarding permitting, design, acquisition of infrastructure, equity and debt funding,

and significant supplier and customer relationship developments.

4. Non-Binding Effect. Other than Fundamental’s agreement to (i) assign, transfer, or

otherwise grant the rights to any permits obtained for the Project to WPPLP if

Fundamental does not provide notice of its intent to close by September 30, 2026, or

does not close by December 31, 2026, and (ii) provide monthly project updates, this

MOU is an expression of the Parties’ present intention and does not create any legatly

binding obligation to consummate the transactions contemplated by the outstanding

commercial terms or to enter into any definitive agreement, except for the mutual

obligation to negotiate in good faith as set forth in Section 2. No Party shall be liable

to the other for any damages, costs, or expenses for the non-binding provisions of this

MOU if negotiations are terminated, for any reason, prior to the execution of definitive

agreements.

5. Governing Law. This MOU shall be governed by and construed in accordance with

the laws of the State of West Virginia, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

Any disputes shall be resolved pursuant to the Dispute Resolution provisions in the

Development Agreement.
